messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx and tail latency spike in ap-southeast-1 (hosts: gcp-apac-1*). 5xx rate: 4.8% over 5m, p95 latency +320ms. Paging oncall.

oncall: I got the page, looking now. First indicator is backend GPU OOM / preemptions? pulling metrics.

aj: copying graphs — looks like gcp-apac-1 node pool had instant CPU steal events starting ~03:02 UTC, coincides with increased queuing. Customers reporting slow generation and some 502s.

maria: Confirmed several deployments started failing KV-cache warmup causing thundering prefix misses. Load on embeddings and reranking spikes.

kevin: Quick question — can we redirect traffic off gcp-apac-1 to gcp-apac-2 while we stabilize? Need to avoid global failover (too disruptive). Recommended: staged reroute of non-enterprise traffic then partial brownout of heavy features.

sriram: Agreed. Plan suggestion (staged):
1) Apply a soft rate-limit (5rps->2rps) per anonymous client group in ap-southeast-1.
2) Disable reranking and long-context pipelines for non-committed tenants in region.
3) Reroute new sessions from gcp-apac-1 -> gcp-apac-2 via traffic-manager staged rule.
4) Drain gcp-apac-1 GPUs (cordon + drain) after traffic shift.

liz: I'm on docs/comms — will prepare customer-facing status once we confirm scope. Do we have a list of impacted customers to DM?

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook invoked: "apac-region-degrade-v2". Steps: 1) execute traffic-manager reroute in staged mode, 2) update quota overrides, 3) enable brownout profile for non-enterprise.

aj: Executing step 1 in staged mode now. Command:```
# staged reroute: shift 30% of new sessions from gcp-apac-1 to gcp-apac-2 over 10m
redwood traffic-manager reroute --region ap-southeast-1 --from gcp-apac-1 --to gcp-apac-2 --staged-percent 30 --duration 10m
```

incident-bot: ACTION ACK — staged reroute started. Change-id: reroute-1782501123-a. Monitoring latency/5xx every 60s.

maria: seeing immediate p95 improvement for the shifted sessions, but gcp-apac-1 still showing high queue depth for long-lived KV loads. Proceed with step 2?

sriram: Yes. Applying brownout: disable features for non-committed customers. Command:```
# brownout profile apply
redwood feature-toggle set --profile apac-brownout-2026-03-15 
  --disable reranking,long-context,structured-output 
  --target group:non-enterprise 
  --note "temporary brownout due to provider instability"
```

kevin: Also push a temporary quota increase for enterprise customers so they can bypass soft rate-limits if needed:```
redwood quotas set --region ap-southeast-1 --group enterprise --qps 50 --note "safeguard during provider reroute"
```

liz: Drafting status page now:
- Impact: increased latency and intermittent 5xx in APAC (ap-southeast-1) affecting non-enterprise chat/generation and batch embeddings.
- Mitigation: staged reroute to alternate APAC provider, selective brownout for non-enterprise, quotas adjusted for enterprise.
- ETA: monitoring; updates every 15m.

oncall: Doing the drain once we confirm 80% of new sessions hit gcp-apac-2 and p95 is stable. Cordon + drain commands ready:```
kubectl cordon node/gcp-apac-1-node-12 && kubectl drain node/gcp-apac-1-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

incident-bot: Update — staged reroute at 30% -> 60% (manual bump) per request. Change-id: reroute-1782501123-b.

aj: bumped to 60% after monitoring stable at 30m mark. New session p95 for shifted traffic ~140ms lower, 5xx down to 1.2% on shifted subset.

maria: Starting selective drain of a single problematic GPU host now (cordon & drain noisy node).

kevin: After draining node, we should keep a temporary provider weight rule to avoid immediate rebalancing back to gcp-apac-1.

sriram: Implemented sticky rule: traffic-manager weight gcp-apac-1=10 gcp-apac-2=90 for 60m.

ops-runbook-bot: Note entry added to incident log: "staged reroute + brownout applied; enterprise quotas adjusted; single-node drain executed."

liz: Sent initial customer DM to top 20 impacted tenants and posted public status at https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1782501123 — flagged as "degraded".

oncall: Handoff — I'm going offline in 25m. @aj you take primary oncall for remainder of incident, @maria you take secondary. Provide runbook link and escalation path.

aj: taking over. Confirming monitoring alerts to my phone and PagerDuty.

maria: I'll watch post-drain metrics and check for cache warmup regressions. If p95 > 500ms or 5xx > 2% region-wide, escalate to infra leads and consider full region failover.

incident-bot: Notice — throttles applied: anonymous group qps lowered to 2, enterprise qps 50 (override), brownout profile active.

kevin: Quick customer note — turned off reranking on non-enterprise; retrieval-only flows maintained. This reduces compute by ~35% on region.

aj: We're seeing sustained improvement: regional 5xx down to 0.9% and overall p95 dropping back toward normal. Continuing to monitor for 60m.

sriram: Post-mitigation steps:
- Keep brownout for at least 2 hours or until provider reports stable.
- Gradual de-escalation: staged reroute reversal at 10% steps every 20m.
- Prepare postmortem draft with kernel/provider preemption data and KV warmup timeline.

liz: Noted — preparing postmortem outline and customers touched list. Will attach logs and runbook steps.

oncall: leaving; thanks team.

aj: final status (18:37 UTC): mitigations healthy, p95 ~normal, 5xx under 1%. Keeping brownout for 90m then reassess. I'll update status and close thread when fully resolved.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS — mitigations applied, degraded -> stabilizing. Next automatic update in 15m.

maria: adding one follow-up — we should cache-warmup proactively on failover in the future and add provider preemption detectors to runtime alerts. Adding as action item to postmortem.

kevin: Agreed — add runbook step to pre-warm KV on reroute start.

aj: acknowledged. Closing handoff: I'm the incident owner for now. Will file postmortem and link in this thread.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident closed for active mitigation phase. Follow-ups scheduled."
